newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline holds steady despite arb, weak NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline holds steady despite arb, weak NYMEX.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were steady to slightly higher despite a closed arbitrage to the States, weaker NYMEX futures and U.S. inventory data showing a healthy build in supplies last week.
Traders said barge prices may be finding a temporary floor due to snugger NWE supplies and a correction from its recent sharp selloff.

Eurograde barges rose $1 to $189/$191 fob ARA. Trades were done at $186 fob ARA, $187 fob AR and at $189. Refinery barrels were heard on offer at $191.50, with the closest bids at $189. One trade house continued to be a noted seller.
One barge trader said the tone of the market had turned less bearish in the last two days, though there was much uncertainty ahead of the NYMEX open and after recent declines.
"The European barge market seems to be comparatively tight," he said. "The market is less tight than everyone wants to believe."
"ARA refiners are not offering too much and out of Scandinavia we're not getting too much material," he said.
He said no cargo prices were heard so far today, with most interest for late-June.

July NYMEX gasoline last traded up 0.20 cent at 56.60 cents a gallon in overnight ACCESS trading after American Petroleum Institute said U.S. inventories last week rose 2.7 million barrels. Stocks now stand at 202.4 million barrels, down 3.4 million from a year ago.
NYMEX futures dropped more than 2.5 cents on Tuesday.
